title: Betti cardinalities in a smooth projective curve family
statement:
Let $S$ be Noetherian
and let $f:X\to S$ be
smooth and
projective, with geometric
fibres of pure dimension one. Fix a prime $\ell$ invertible on $S$.
Write $c_s$ for the number of connected components of the
smooth proper curve $X_{\bar s}$, and
$g_s=\sum_D g(D)$ for the sum of the
genera over its connected components.
Then the etale cohomology
cardinalities are

$$
|H^r(X_{\bar s},\mathbf F_\ell)|=
\begin{cases}
\ell^{c_s},&r=0,2,\\
\ell^{2g_s},&r=1,\\
1,&r>2,
\end{cases}
$$

and each of these functions of $s$ is constructible.

proof.text: Fix $s\in S$, set $k=\overline{\kappa(s)}$, and put $C=X_{\bar s}$. By [lem-pc-projective-proper], $f$ is proper. Apply [lem-pc-proper-base-change] to $\operatorname{Spec}k\to S$: the structure map $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth and proper. Properness includes separatedness and finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The pure-dimension-one hypothesis implies $\dim C\leq1$, so $C$ is a smooth curve in [def-sc-curves]; the empty fibre is allowed.

Apply [lem-sbc-smooth-curve-points-decomposition] to $C$. It gives a finite disjoint decomposition into open-and-closed smooth connected one-dimensional curves $D_i$ and points $\operatorname{Spec}k$. A point summand would be an irreducible component of dimension zero: it is clopen, and no irreducible subset can meet two disjoint clopen summands. This contradicts purity, so there are no point summands. The $D_i$ are precisely the connected components, since they are connected and clopen and cover $C$. Thus $|I|=c_s$. Each $D_i$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](c), applied to its closed immersion into the proper $C$.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives], embed $\mathcal O_C$ into an injective $I^0$, embed its cokernel into an injective $I^1$, and repeat on successive cokernels. The differential $I^n\to I^{n+1}$ is the quotient map onto the preceding cokernel followed by its chosen embedding; its kernel is the preceding image. This constructs an injective resolution $\mathcal O_C\to I^\bullet$. By [lem-sc-ringed-space-restrict-injective-resolution], its restriction to each open $D_i$ is an injective resolution of $\mathcal O_{D_i}$. In each degree the sheaf gluing axiom on the disjoint open cover gives $\Gamma(C,I^n)=\prod_i\Gamma(D_i,I^n|_{D_i})$, with differentials acting coordinatewise. The kernel of a coordinatewise map is the product of its kernels, and its image is the product of its images (choose a preimage in each of the finitely many coordinates). Writing $Z_i^r$ and $B_i^r$ for component cycles and boundaries, the map $\prod_i Z_i^r\to\prod_i(Z_i^r/B_i^r)$ is surjective (choose representatives in each coordinate) with kernel $\prod_i B_i^r$. Hence its quotient, the cohomology of the product complex, is the product of the component cohomologies. With the injective-resolution definition [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], this yields $H^r(C,\mathcal O_C)\cong\bigoplus_i H^r(D_i,\mathcal O_{D_i})$ for every $r\geq0$, as $k$-vector spaces: the restriction and gluing maps are $k$-linear. For $I=\varnothing$ the global-sections complex is zero.

For every $D_i$, [lem-sc-global-functions] gives $H^0(D_i,\mathcal O_{D_i})=k$: its final clause applies directly to a proper smooth connected curve. By [def-sc-genus], $\dim_kH^1(D_i,\mathcal O_{D_i})=g(D_i)$. Taking dimensions in step 3, by concatenating bases of the finitely many summands, gives $h^0(C,\mathcal O_C)=c_s$ and $h^1(C,\mathcal O_C)=\sum_i g(D_i)=g_s$. The empty sum is zero.

proof.text: The already proved properness of $f$ implies finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Since $S$ is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian, in particular locally Noetherian. The structure module $\mathcal O_X$ is quasi-coherent and of finite type: on $\operatorname{Spec}A$ it is $\widetilde A$, and the identity is a surjection from one copy of $\mathcal O_X$. These are the conditions of [pqf-def-coherent]. Hence [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] makes $\mathcal O_X$ coherent. By [lem-pc-smooth-flat], $f$ is flat. The definition [def-weil-flat-morphism] says exactly that the stalk $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S,f(x)}$ for every $x$, so the structure module is flat over $S$.

Apply [lem-fin-projective-flat-coherent-ranks] to the original projective $f:X\to S$ and $\mathcal G=\mathcal O_X$. Its coherence and flatness over $S$ were verified in step 5, and $S$ is Noetherian by hypothesis. The fibre module is $\mathcal O_{X_{\bar s}}$, since on affine charts the base-change tensor product of the structure module is the structure module of the fibre. In degrees zero and one the theorem gives constructibility of $h^0(X_{\bar s},\mathcal O)$ and $h^1(X_{\bar s},\mathcal O)$. Step 4 identifies these functions with $c_s$ and $g_s$, respectively.

The prime $\ell$ is a unit in $k$, because it is invertible on $S$. Apply [lem-sc-primitive-root] with $n=\ell$ to choose a primitive root $\zeta\in k$. Each $D_i$ is smooth, proper, connected, nonempty and one-dimensional over the algebraically closed $k$ by steps 1-2. Therefore [thm-sc-proper-cohomology], with this primitive-root trivialization, gives component cohomology isomorphic to $\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$, $(\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z)^{2g(D_i)}$, and $\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$ in degrees zero, one, and two, respectively, and zero above two. Only the abstract groups and their cardinalities are used; no choice of roots needs to vary with $s$.

By [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant], the restriction of the constant abelian sheaf $\mathbf F_\ell$ to $D_i$ is the same constant sheaf on $D_i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct-cohomology-assembly] to the finite clopen decomposition in step 2. It identifies $H^r(C,\mathbf F_\ell)$ with the product of the component cohomology groups computed in step 7. A tuple in a product of $a$ copies of $\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$ has $\ell$ independent choices in each coordinate, hence cardinality $\ell^a$. Thus the degree-zero and degree-two groups have cardinality $\ell^{|I|}=\ell^{c_s}$, the degree-one group has cardinality $\ell^{\sum_i2g(D_i)}=\ell^{2g_s}$, and above degree two the product of zero groups is the zero group, of cardinality one. An empty product is also a one-element group, giving the asserted formula for empty fibres.

proof.text: By constructibility in step 6 there are finite constructible partitions on which $c_s$ and $g_s$ are constant. Their common refinement consists of the pairwise intersections of their pieces, which are constructible by [def-weil-constructible-subset]. On each refined piece the functions $\ell^{c_s}$ and $\ell^{2g_s}$ are constant. They therefore are constructible functions; the constant function one is constructible as well. This proves the required constructibility for every fixed degree $r$.
